articles.title: Madueke breaks Nottingham Forest’s resistance as dogged Arsenal edge to victory
articles.summary: The theme before kick-off was blanks. Or, more precisely, whether either team could stop firing them at the City Ground. It is a detail to make Oliver Glasner extremely uncomfortable that his Nottingham Forest team had still to score at their home stadium.
body: Forest’s frustrations under their new manager go on. It was another spirited performance from them, bits to like, especially a full throttle performance from Liam Delap in the No 9 position. But, for the fifth time under Glasner in all competitions, there was not a goal to celebrate in front of the club’s home fans.

It was a game that came to feel increasingly set up for the famous terrace chant. One-nil to the Ars-en-nal. Or, as the travelling hordes would have it, one-nil to the champions. Arsenal did not play well. They created little, finishing with just one shot of target. How Noni Madueke made it count.

On as a half-time substitute, the winger took a pass from Declan Rice in the 80th minute and had only one thing on his mind. To cut inside from the left and unload. The connection was pure and that was when he caught a break, which he has worked to earn after a difficult start to the season. The ball deflected off Jair Cunha and flew past the Forest goalkeeper, Matz Sels.

articles.title: ‘Like a fresh start’: Michael Carrick relieved by Manchester United’s draw at Leeds
articles.summary: Head coach insists ‘we can still have a really good season’ ‘We were the dominant side,’ says Farke. After a week in which Michael Carrick had “the headphones on” to quieten the noise, Manchester United’s head coach claimed Sunday’s 1-1 draw at Leeds “felt like a fresh start” and insisted that the…
body: Carrick’s team have seven points from seven Premier League games and have won only once in the competition, against Ipswich in August. Sunday’s draw followed the previous weekend’s 1-1 draw with Tottenham.

Yet after a week in which United lost 2-0 at Atlético Madrid, after which Lisandro Martínez criticised the recruitment of the director of football, Jason Wilcox, Carrick was relieved at the point against Daniel Farke’s team.

“[It’s been] quite quiet inside [the club] – the headphones have been on this week. It felt like a bit of a fresh start today – where we’re at and accepting it and doing something about it,” said the manager. “That didn’t surprise me today. We’re not getting too carried away because we haven’t won the game, but if you keep doing the right things for the right reasons then you get what you deserve in the end.”

body: Osmand netted twice in three first-half minutes in the first meeting of the teams since his goal sealed Celtic’s last-gasp title success at the expense of the Edinburgh side.

The Hoops were two up inside 10 minutes after Kieran Tierney and Benjamin Nygren both scored from Mika Baur corners, and the latter had the Premiership champions 5-1 up at the interval after forcing an own goal from Jamie McCart.
Camilo Durán piled on the agony with a goal four minutes after the restart and Nygren rounded off the scoring to send Martin O’Neill’s side four points clear of Rangers.
Hearts had arrived in Glasgow as the division’s top goalscorers and with the opportunity to move two points behind the leaders.

articles.title: Evanilson swivels his hips to seal Bournemouth win against 10-man Sunderland
articles.summary: Bournemouth’s, and Marco Rose’s, wait for a Premier League win is over. Sunderland, locked in the bottom three, are becoming this season’s object lesson in travelling too far, too fast.
body: Once Kevin Danso was dismissed in the 17th minute for the denial of a goalscoring opportunity, Sunderland were sunk. If Evanilson was the match-winner with a goal, an assist and as the player Danso fouled, Régis Le Bris’s team were architects of their own downfall. “A bad day, a bad start,” the Sunderland manager said. Sixth and seventh last season, both teams have struggled domestically while cruising in the Europa League but Sunderland’s troubles deepened.

There was mitigation on offer. With a tight turnaround from Leiria on Thursday, England’s south coast on Sunday and Poznan in midweek, Wearside resources are stretched. And their European dream comes against uncomfortable domestic realities. Talk of a possible sale continues, a boardroom reshuffle placing Kyril Louis-Dreyfus, the youthful majority owner, in charge of day‑to‑day operations. On the pitch, Sunderland have not had a league win since August, and lost four in succession.

Both teams had made five changes from Thursday and Bournemouth, who had beaten Sturm Graz at home, were visibly fresher. “Fatigue for me is not an issue,” Le Bris said. “We just have to get used to it.”

articles.title: St Brigid's secure historic first Antrim football title
articles.summary: St Brigid's make history in an all-Belfast Antrim SFC final, securing their first senior football title with a 0-21 to 1-16 win over O'Donovan Rossa.
body: After a nervy start for St Brigid's, who were playing in their first final, they found their way into the game thanks to Ronan McGrady's scores and they led by two points at half-time.
Despite Diarmuid Rogan's goal for Rossa early in the period, St Brigid's, who were founded in 1998, held on and came out victorious with a two-point win over their cross-city rivals.
O'Donovan Rossa made a great start as Stephen Beatty struck an early two-pointer.
Corey Walsh curled over a brilliant point to make it 0-7 to 0-4 in his side's favour after 15 minutes with St Brigid's struggling to get a foothold in the game.

articles.title: Mbeumo offers Carrick solace as Man Utd winless run goes on
articles.summary: Michael Carrick said he had his headphones on this week so didn't hear the noise around Manchester United, but a 1-1 draw at Leeds means it is six games without a win.
body: In a season that is forcing Manchester United fans to dig deep for reasons to be positive, Bryan Mbeumo scored again at Elland Road.
That is four goals in seven Premier League games for the Cameroon forward.
Apart from Bruno Fernandes, who scored a hat-trick against Ipswich in August, no-one else in Michael Carrick's squad has scored more than one.

But it's meagre fare. It is true to say Manchester United did reasonably well in their 1-1 draw at Leeds United, just as they did at Atletico Madrid on Tuesday after conceding inside the first minute.

articles.title: Spurs' boisterous Keldon Johnson feels even more energetic after makeover
articles.summary: Spurs forward Keldon Johnson was at his high-energy best both during and after Friday night's 126-97 preseason-ending victory over Sacramento. After finishing with 15 points, five rebounds and two assists in 20 minutes, the 2026 Sixth Man of the Year held court in the locker room, entertaining…
body: When he finally left the Frost Bank Center wearing an orange-and-white Texas ball cap, he looked he still had plenty left in his tank to work late into the night doing chores at his Boerne ranch if needed.

After losing at least 15 pounds in the offseason, the 6-foot-6, 215-pound Johnson is raring to go and ready to prove the slimmed-down version of himself can be just as robust as the one that produced 13.2 points, 5.4 rebounds and 1.4 assists while becoming the only NBA player in 2025-26 to play in all 82 games without a start.
"I feel like I'm better," the eighth-year pro and longest-tenured current Spur said when asked about his makeover.

"All-around game, I'm faster, just as strong. I feel like it's just staying this weight and staying disciplined is the most important thing. And I feel like I can do that. Obviously, I was a little bit heavier last year, but I like where I'm at. Like I said, I'm moving good, my body feels good. And, overall, I just feel like I'm a better player when I'm lighter."

articles.summary: (This story has been updated to add new information.) For Northeast Florida, playoff time is now. Beachside made history as the Jacksonville area's first-ever qualifier for an Open Division tournament in any sport, highlighting the Florida High School Athletic Association's bracket release on Oct.
body: The eight-team Open Division includes the highest-rated teams across all states and all classes in the FHSAA ranking system. The top eight are split into Pool A (Nos. 1, 4, 5 and 8) and Pool B (Nos. 2, 3, 6 and 7). Beachside landed the No. 6 seed overall.

The regional tournaments across six standard classes, the Rural class and the new eight-team Open Division all lead to November's FHSAA final four tournament in Winter Haven. There, Northeast Florida schools will be chasing down the area's first championship since Middleburg in 2023.

The FHSAA used its ranking formula to hand out at-large berths, four per region per class for Classes 1A through 6A, who qualify for postseason along with the champions of each district. Seeds are based on the association's rankings formula.
Classes 1A through 3A begin their regionals on Oct. 20, followed by 4A through 6A and the Open Division on Oct. 21 and the Rural class on Oct. 24.

articles.title: College football chaos - 5 top eight teams fall in Week 7
articles.summary: College football needed only one Saturday to completely change the national picture. Five of the top eight teams in the AP poll lost during Week 7, marking the first time that has happened since 1989. No. 1 Georgia and No.
body: The chaos directly affects Texas A&M. Alabama, Tennessee and Texas remain on the Aggies’ schedule, and each looked much different by the end of Saturday. Those games are still challenging, but none feel as predictable as they once did.
A&M has plenty of its own problems to solve after an inconsistent first half of the season. However, Week 7 showed that no team is safe and reopened the College Football Playoff picture.
Auburn erased an early 14-point deficit and stunned Georgia in Athens on Alex McPherson’s 34-yard field goal as time expired.
The Tigers scored 24 unanswered points before Georgia rallied to tie in the fourth quarter. Gunner Stockton then fumbled on Georgia’s final possession, giving Auburn the chance to complete the upset.

articles.title: Arsenal win with one shot on target as Forest sink into bottom three
articles.summary: Arsenal's only shot on target proved enough to snatch victory at Nottingham Forest through Noni Madueke's deflected strike, keeping the champions within touching distance of Premier League leaders Manchester City and condemning Forest to the relegation zone.
body: After 80 frustrating minutes at the City Ground, substitute Madueke cut inside from the left and fired towards goal. His strike deflected off Jair Cunha, wrong-footed Matz Sels and found the net to settle a game in which Arsenal had struggled to turn possession into chances.

Arsenal had dominated the ball but registered no shots on target in the first half. Kai Havertz headed wide from a Declan Rice free-kick while Gabriel's set-piece effort was cleared almost off the line by Ousmane Diomande.

Forest made life difficult for Mikel Arteta's side, defending resolutely and threatening on the counter. Murillo almost salvaged a point in stoppage time with a superb solo run, driving at the Arsenal defence before curling narrowly wide. Ezri Konsa then made a crucial late challenge to deny Liam Delap.
However, despite their opportunities, it was the same old story for Oliver Glasner's side, who failed to find a breakthrough.

articles.title: Texans beat Jags in final seconds of Wembley thriller
articles.summary: Ka'imi Fairbairn kicked a 49-yard field goal as time expired to lift the Houston Texans to a 34-31 victory over the Jacksonville Jaguars in a thriller at Wembley Stadium on Sunday.
body: It was a game that began with referee Larry Smith being carted off with a non-contact injury in the opening seconds. A game that spent its interval staging on-field Corgi races. And a game that concluded with another dose of boot-fuelled drama following Cam Little's last-second winner against the Philadelphia Eagles at Tottenham the previous week.
Texans quarterback CJ Stroud threw for 312 yards and three touchdowns while Jaylin Noel led his side with four receptions for 107 yards and a score as Houston improved to 2-4 on the year.

Stroud's first interception of the season came by way of Travis Hunter as the two-way Jags star became the first player to score a touchdown and record a pick in the same game since Brian Dawkins for the Philadelphia Eagles against the Texans on September 29, 2002.
Trevor Lawrence finished 24 of 41 for 306 yards, four touchdowns and one interception as the Jaguars slipped to 4-2 at the end of their fortnight in the UK.

articles.title: Man Utd held by Leeds as winless run continues
articles.summary: Manchester United delivered a more committed performance in a changed formation but were held to a 1-1 draw by Leeds as pressure on Michael Carrick continues to grow.
body: In a week that included defeat to Atletico Madrid and an explosive interview from Lisandro Martinez - who started at Elland Road - the noise was calmed somewhat by a display that showed character, if not enough quality to claim a second league win of the season.
United played without a recognised striker for the majority, allowing Youri Tielemans a more offensive role and he combined with Bryan Mbeumo to open the scoring in the first half.
But Carrick's side faded badly as the game went on, another fixture in which they were outrun, eventually pegged back by an instinctive Dominic Calvert-Lewin strike from a poorly defended corner.

Leeds away was pitched as the worst game to end a fractious week. In reality, it forced United to scrap and that at least appeared to show appetite for the fight. "In isolation, going to Leeds and performing how they did was a decent result," reflected Jamie Carragher. They were helped by the fact that Daniel Farke's side were not at their battling best either.
